# Independent audit: flat symmetric rounding and joint escape


candidate 6f9d37b455a5cd1c,
rechecked the needed identities in
candidate 30d7d56bee7b8657, and reran the
rounded verifier with work/math-venv/bin/python. No mathematical
repair is needed.

The result concerns one selected concurrent cap group and an actual
compatible finite fiber family. It does not preserve unselected cap
budgets or prove a general mixed-integer depth bound.

## 1. Symmetry, coordinates, and actual strict compatibility

The shear uses a real functional v with v.p=1, changes no integer
base, has continuous fiber Jacobian one, and commutes with global
reflection. It centers both selected simplex fibers simultaneously.
The cap sign at p is lambda_i>=a_i, and summing the d+1 margins
gives zero exactly. Coverage therefore holds in the entire ambient
space throughout every threshold motion.

The boundary of each selected cap is null on every full-dimensional
fiber. Global central symmetry implies its entire original-source
mass is M/2 for every nearby a. This statement does not require
individual other-fiber contributions to be constant or smooth.

For excluded-target representations, the quadratic base profile
has the exact Jensen gap sum theta_w |w-z|^2. Adding the unit ball
multiplies this by epsilon in every unit direction. The minimum
base separation gives a uniform positive bound over all real
barycentric representations, not merely their vertices. Removing
a positive selfweight and renormalizing is valid.

Independent Hausdorff changes alter each support gap by at most
twice their size. Thus the prescribed radius epsilon Delta_P^2/4
is a valid strict-inclusion neighborhood. Positivity of all
perturbed fibers is retained by choosing the eventual physical
motion sufficiently small; the selected rounded fibers already
have positive interior balls. The exact convex-hull fiber argument
uses all anchored inclusions and lattice completeness. No
compatibility constraint at an unlisted integer base is discarded.

The common normalization alpha_epsilon is positive, tends to one,
preserves all inclusions and central symmetry, and gives total
mass exactly M. Hence the preliminary normalized step preserves
all nonvertical through-origin cap budgets exactly.

## 2. Exact face-tube regularity, including moving caps

The claimed polynomial property is correct under the explicitly
stated uniform one-positive-vertex sign pattern. It is not a
general assertion for arbitrary cuts through moving vertices.

For a simplex and every sufficiently small parallel radius, the
nearest-point decomposition partitions the parallel body into
orthogonal products of a face and its truncated normal cone,
up to null boundaries. The normal cone is perpendicular to the
face's tangent space, so the product Jacobian is one.

A face without the positive vertex stays uniformly outside the
cap. For a face containing that vertex, its cap fraction is exactly
the kth power of the positive height divided by the k positive
height differences. A normal displacement adds the same value
u.w to every height, so it leaves all denominator differences
unchanged. The fixed sign margins and a common upper bound on
|u| ensure this formula is valid uniformly for all small w and
all parameters in a common neighborhood. The k=0 vertex sector
and the full-dimensional k=d face are treated correctly.

An affine image A_W of the reference simplex transforms each
normal cone by A_W^(-T), including its linear span. On that
normal space the polar Jacobian is exactly

    J_W tau^q |L_W theta|^(-q) r^(q-1) dr d sigma(theta).

The power q, the subspace Jacobian, and the absence of any face
area factor in this normal Jacobian are correct. Face area is
already supplied separately in the retained-face formula.
The reference spherical cone is fixed and has finite measure,
also when q=1 and its sphere has counting measure. Invertibility
of A_W gives uniform upper and lower bounds on all denominators.

Expansion of the degree-k retained-area numerator gives powers
tau^(q+j), 0<=j<=k, hence degree at most d. Coefficients and all
parameter derivatives are smooth under fixed-domain integration.
Only the full-dimensional face has a nonzero tau^0 term, equal
to the original simplex cap. This proves the stated uniform C2
convergence with O(tau) error, for changing W, u, and b.

The volume assertion is the same decomposition without clipping.
The coefficient formulas give a polynomial extension in the
radius to negative values for the purposes of ordinary IFT; no
negative-radius body is needed. Smooth curvature of the rounded
boundary is not used, and the retained flat faces cause no gap.

## 3. Cancellation and the exact implicit correction

For every a, the unchanged rounded symmetric source has mass
Mhat_epsilon/2 in each selected cap. Changing only the selected
fiber therefore gives the exact global identity

    cap mass = Mhat_epsilon/2
               +F_epsilon(W,a)-F_epsilon(I,a).

In particular its pure threshold derivatives cancel identically.
No derivative of an individual arbitrary nonsimplex fiber is
required. The selected-fiber volume and cap increments satisfy
the joint smoothness furnished by the face-tube argument.

I rechecked the physical right inverse: S maps to zero-column-sum
matrices and its normalized cap derivative is the requested
vector. Dividing its input by the original simplex volume V
is exactly the needed right inverse for absolute cap volumes.
Thus the r-Jacobian is the identity at zero rounding.

The implicit system has the branch r(0,epsilon)=0 because its
cap increments vanish at W=I for every a and epsilon. Its t
derivative at (0,0) is zero because B0 lies in the cap-gradient
kernel and all pure threshold derivatives vanish.

The simplex Lagrangian has zero full first derivative and joint
Hessian VQ, where

    Q=(d-1)/d [2-1/(d+1)]>0.

Differentiating the exact cap equalities twice cancels the
correction acceleration against the objective-one multipliers.
The resulting reduced objective second derivative is precisely
VQ. Joint C2 convergence, together with the invertible constraint
Jacobian, makes this reduced second derivative continuous in
epsilon and positive for all sufficiently small positive radii.

No false stationarity of the rounded objective is inferred. Even
if its first derivative is nonzero, its symmetric second
difference is positive for sufficiently small t, so at least
one sign gives positive volume at exact original cap budgets.
Fixing epsilon first and then taking t arbitrarily small is
essential: it places the physical displacement inside the
O(epsilon) actual compatibility neighborhood.

At that nearby point, surjectivity persists. A further small
implicit correction to the target vector -eta times the all-ones
vector reduces every selected cap. Continuity preserves the
strict volume gain and the open compatibility conditions.
This step is an individual-budget improvement, not merely a
weighted-sum improvement.

## 4. Normalization, support reductions, and scope

The final common dilation multiplies every actual mass by
alpha_epsilon^d. It sends Mhat_epsilon to M and Mhat_epsilon/2
to D=M/2, leaving the strict gain and every cap decrease strict.
The transformed cap coefficient is

    l_i(x)-alpha_epsilon(a_i-1/m)(v.z),

with the displayed sign and scale. The margins continue to sum
to zero, and all continuous normals stay nonzero.

Taking the positive-fiber hull preserves the original mixed
measure, and its positive base set is lattice-complete by
Brunn-Minkowski. In the lower-rank case the saturated base lattice
admits the stated unimodular normalization. A transverse base
cube of side less than one has only the zero transverse integer
coordinate, so the explicit ambient completion creates no
additional positive integer fibers. The source carefully avoids
claiming Hausdorff approximation of arbitrary discarded real-base
parts of the original body.

Dimension one is correctly excluded by the zero joint Hessian.
There is no imposed bound on the number of physical facets; the
rounding itself usually leaves that class. Only the chosen
d+1-cap group is controlled.

## 5. Verifier and its precise evidentiary scope

The command

    work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_flat_symmetric_rounding_joint_escape.py

passes. Standard system Python lacks mpmath; this is an environment
dependency, not a failed mathematical check.

The script checks the planar physical right inverse and critical
Hessian exactly using rational arithmetic. Its separately
implemented edge-strip and vertex-sector formula agrees with
the face-tube proof. At zero rounding it recovers reduced
curvature 5/12 for the area-1/2 reference triangle. Its additional
rounded curvatures and active-midpoint feasible path are
high-precision numerical consistency checks, correctly described
as such; they are not used to establish the all-dimensional
theorem or IFT existence.

The mathematical proof of all-d regularity is Section 3's exact
face decomposition, and the mathematical proof of escape is
Section 5's ordinary IFT and positive reduced second variation.
There is no OC dependency or circular use of the desired
improvement.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
